rust.summary:
Phase P1a is done: the cell and sheet storage from design §2.2 and the raw member copy from §2.11. The yggdryl crate builds cleanly, and every settle command passes, including the openpyxl exchange in both directions.

Cell (`excel/cell.rs`):
- Field order is value, reference, formula, style, kind, format, error. `const _: () = assert!(size_of::<Cell>() <= 80)` holds, and the actual size is 80 bytes.
- New public `ExcelError` with the 19 variants. `as_str` spells each one, and `Unrecognized` answers `#UNRECOGNIZED`. `from_text` ignores ASCII case and maps any other text to `Unrecognized`. It also implements Display.
- The SmolStr `with_formula`/`formula` and `with_error`/`error` are deleted. In their place: `with_formula(Formula)`, `formula() -> Option<&Formula>`, `with_error(ExcelError)`, `error() -> Option<ExcelError>`, `error_text()`, `with_style(StyleId)` and `style()`.
- An `Unrecognized` error keeps its literal in the value slot. `value()` and `into_scalar()` answer null for any error cell, `is_null()` is true for them, and `text()` gives the error text.
- New crate-private helpers: `written_error` and `move_to`.

StyleId (`excel/style.rs`, new): `StyleId(u16)` with `DEFAULT`, `new`, `as_u16`, `from_attribute`, `From<u16>` and `From<StyleId> for u32`.

Formula (`excel/formula.rs`, new, interim): `Formula(Arc<Shape>)`, where `Shape` holds the file text as one verbatim run. It has `from_file(text, host)` (never fails), `at(host) -> impl Display`, equality and hashing by text, and Debug.

Sheet (`excel/sheet.rs`):
- `Row` is now a `Vec<Cell>` sorted by column and binary-searched.
- `Sheet` gains:
  - `extent`: a 64 KiB box of per-column counters that exists only while the sheet holds a cell. It makes `cell_count()` O(1), `dimension()` O(log rows) and `extend_from_serie` linear.
  - `extras`: a sparse `BTreeMap<CellRef, CellExtra>` holding `cm`, `vm` and `ph`. An entry moves with its cell through set/insert/remove cell, insert/remove rows, slice and `write_serie`.
  - `revision()`: moved by every `&mut` change; `cell_mut` counts as a change.
- Sheet equality ignores revision and extent. `set_date_system` and `set_state` are no longer `const`.
- Parsing reuses the parser's row buffer through a new `recycle` step and gives each row an exact-capacity vector.
- The part writer reads the file's `s` into each cell's StyleId and writes it back, along with `cm`, `vm` and `ph`.
- The `unreachable!` is now a typed refusal naming the cell, and so is an `Unrecognized` error with no literal to write.
- An empty formula is never written as `<f></f>`. A shared-formula dependent keeps its cached value and holds no formula (interim until P2; a test names this).
- The rustdoc states the held-state bounds.

Parser: reads `r`, `t`, `s`, `cm`, `vm` and `ph` in one pass over the attributes. It refuses, naming the cell, an `s` that is not an integer from 0 to 65,535 and a malformed `cm`, `vm` or `ph`. The record path reads through the same parser, so it refuses the same way.

ZIP: `ZipArchive::copy_member_from(&self, source: &Arc<ZipArchive>, path) -> Result<ZipEntry>` copies the stored bytes one batch at a time and keeps the method, CRC-32, sizes, restart map and the record's other facts. It never decodes or re-encodes. The two archive locks are always taken in the same order, so copies in both directions at once cannot deadlock. Copying a member into its own archive just returns the existing entry.

Tests added: `excel/{style,formula}.rs`, extensions to `cell.rs`, `sheet.rs` and `parser.rs`, `zip/archive.rs`, an iobase_calls row for the copy, and allocation pins (`excel_cell_is_at_most_80_bytes`, a re-pinned per-row cost, `excel_sheet_parse_costs_nothing_per_cell`, and a StyleId read with no allocation).

Style write-back is guarded until P1b: a non-temporal cell writes its StyleId only when the index is below the style offset, meaning it is one of the opened package's own cellXfs. A package built from nothing writes no `s` for such a cell. Temporal cells still get the crate's own temporal format entry at style_index + offset, as today. Without the guard, a StyleId carried in from another workbook could point at a cellXfs entry the written styles part does not hold. A pinned test covers this (`a_style_index_the_written_styles_part_does_not_hold_is_not_written`).

The parser refuses any `s` that is not a decimal integer from 0 to 65535, not only values above 65,535; non-numeric text used to read as 0. `styles::a_style_index_past_cellxfs_is_general` now uses s=65535, and a new refusal test covers 65536 on both the sheet path and the record path.

CellExtra holds only what P1a reads and writes: cm, vm and ph. The design's shared_string, inline_runs and formula-attribute fields belong to P2; declaring them now would be dead code and fail clippy.

Additions not listed in the design: `StyleId::new`, `StyleId::from_attribute` (same pattern as `CellKind::from_attribute` and `SheetState::from_attribute`), `From<u16> for StyleId`, `From<StyleId> for u32`, `Display for ExcelError`, and a public `Sheet::revision()` (design §2.3 reads it).
`ExcelError::from_text` ignores ASCII case, so `#n/a` reads as NA and is written back as `#N/A`.

`Cell::value()` and `into_scalar()` answer null for every error cell, `Unrecognized` included. The literal stays in the value slot for storage only and is reachable through `error_text()`, so an error never shows up as a value in into_serie or scalar.

Round-trip tests in excel/sheet.rs and excel/workbook.rs now compare cells with the style set aside. They also assert that a temporal cell reads back with the crate's own format index as its StyleId, because the written `s` is now read back instead of discarded.

The allocation pin `excel_sheet_costs_per_row_and_nothing_per_cell` was re-pinned with its reason stated. Laying out and parsing now cost under 5/4 of an allocation per row (measured about 1.17), down from bounds of 2 and 3 per row. A new SheetRows::recycle hands the parser's row buffer back, so parsing costs one exact vector per row. The two cost pins that moved (iobase_calls and allocations excel rows) moved down, and each move is explained by the change.

side.summary:
I built the P1 browser UI foundation in `cli/assets/excel/`. It is vanilla ES modules with no framework, build step or CDN, and it is CSP-clean: no inline style or script, and styles are set only through the CSSOM. All ten modules pass `node --check`. The browser check against the scratchpad dev server passes 26 of 26 steps with no console errors, and the Node unit smoke passes 11 of 11.

**What each file does:**
- `index.html`: the app shell.
  - Title bar reading "‹file› — yggdryl workbook".
  - Ribbon with File (backstage), Home, Insert, Formulas, Data and View tabs, each laid out per §10, with every control carrying a `data-command`.
  - Name Box and formula bar, both read-only for now.
  - The grid host, with a vertical drawn scrollbar and a sheet bar holding the tabs and the horizontal drawn scrollbar.
  - Status bar and toast host.
- `styles.css`: the layout, plus the canvas palette as CSS custom properties. The renderer reads it through `.palette-*` probes. Under `forced-colors` it switches to system colours; the probes carry `forced-color-adjust: none` so they report those colours. Reduced motion is honoured.
- `icons.svg`: our own 54-symbol sprite. Opened on its own, the file renders the logo, so it also serves as the favicon.
- `js/geometry.js`: `Axis` holds a default size plus override runs, with prefix deltas so position↔index is a binary search. It also handles hidden spans and a hidden tail. Also here:
  - `Merges`, bucketed by row tile and expanded to a fixed point.
  - `Geometry`, which converts widths with §4.2's formula and heights as points × 96/72.
  - `Viewport`, which builds the four frozen quadrants and does hit testing and paging.
  - A1 helpers.
- `js/api.js`: moves the token from the URL fragment to `sessionStorage` and strips it with `replaceState`. Every request sends `X-Yggdryl-Token`. Also:
  - RFC 9457 problems become toasts; a 409 `stale_base` raises a `stale` event.
  - `edit()` carries the base revision; downloads are fetched as blobs.
- `js/tiles.js`: 64×32 data tiles in an LRU of 256 that never evicts a shown tile. Shown tiles are fetched before the one-tile prefetch ring, with at most 6 requests in flight. Stale tiles revalidate with `If-None-Match` and keep their cells on a 304. A generation reset drops everything.
- `js/styles.js`: the append-only `styles?from=N` cache. Styles are normalized once (fills with pattern blends, border widths and dashes); CSS font strings are cached per zoom and use the §10 font stack.
- `js/render.js` (`Painter`), drawn per quadrant in this order:
  1. gridlines, then fills and merges painted over the lines they hide;
  2. overflow text laid out (left, right and centered, including text entering from cells off-screen), erasing the gridlines it crosses;
  3. borders, never across a merge's interior;
  4. text: `####`, the `shorter` General spellings, `*` fill, wrap, shrink, indent, underline and strike;
  5. selection shading, the active range border and the fill handle;
  6. headers with selection highlights, the frozen split lines, and a chartsheet message.
- `js/grid.js`: scroll state (`topRow`/`rowOffset`, `leftColumn`/`columnOffset`) and drawn scrollbars (thumb drag, track paging). Also:
  - Input: wheel and touch pan; pointer selection of cells, headers and the corner, with Ctrl/Shift and drag auto-scroll.
  - `ensureVisible`, repainting on the next animation frame, and `data-pending`/`data-frame` markers for tests.
- `js/selection.js`: active cell, multi-range and the far corner. Merges are handled whole; arrows skip hidden lines; Shift-extension grows past merges; Tab and Enter walk the selection (Enter returns to the column Tab started in); whole rows, columns and select-all.
- `js/keyboard.js`: the §10 navigation keys (list below). `use()` lets later phases put their key handlers first.
- `js/a11y.js` (`Mirror`): a visually hidden `role=grid` mirroring the visible window. It carries `aria-rowcount`/`aria-colcount` and row, column and span indices, plus `aria-selected` and `aria-activedescendant`. Each cell also has `data-ref` and its canvas rectangle, and there is an `aria-live` region. It is the focus target and the test oracle.
- `js/main.js`: boot, the command registry (unimplemented commands are no-ops; `download`, `zoom`, `gridlines` and tab scrolling work) and ribbon tabs. It also holds the sheet tab strip (display and switching), per-sheet saved scroll and selection, layout revalidation by ETag, and the Name Box ("4R x 3C" while dragging) and formula bar, which shows the cell's entry from `cells/{ref}`.

Keyboard keys implemented: arrows, Shift and Ctrl+Shift arrows, Ctrl+arrows through `/edge`, Home, Ctrl+Home, Ctrl+End, PgUp/PgDn, Alt+PgUp/PgDn, Tab and Shift+Tab, Enter and Shift+Enter, Ctrl+PgUp/PgDn, Ctrl+A (region through `/edge?direction=region`, then the whole sheet), Ctrl+Space and Shift+Space.

`.gitattributes` gains `cli/assets/** text eol=lf`.

**Scratchpad tooling (not committed):**
- `ui/gen_fixtures.py` writes `ui/fixtures/*.json` from §8.3's examples. The workbook has sheets Data, Chart1 (chartsheet), Report, Far and Secret (hidden), 31 styles and 3,386 cells. It includes §8.3's exact tile example in Report tile 0/0 and the §8.3 cells example at Data!D2, plus a frozen row on Data, frozen rows and columns on Report, and hidden rows and columns.
- `ui/dev.py` serves the working tree at `/` and answers `/api/*` from the fixtures. It follows the contract's ETag/304 behaviour, computes `edge` and region Excel-style, sends the §8.2 headers and requires the token header. Edits are refused with 422.
- Also `ui/check.js` (Playwright), `ui/unit.mjs`, `ui/shot.js`, `ui/restart.sh`, `ui/eslint.config.mjs`, and screenshots `ui/shots/01..11`.

**Verified in Chromium:**
- The token flow; the mirror counts and cell texts (merged-over and hidden cells are absent).
- Arrows skipping hidden rows 8–10; stepping over merges; formula-bar entries.
- Ctrl+arrows, including XFD1 → XFD1048576; Ctrl+Home/End with frozen panes; Shift extension into a merge; Tab and Enter.
- PgDn and Alt+PgDn; Ctrl+A twice; Ctrl+Space and Shift+Space; click, Shift+click, Ctrl+click multi-range, and drag.
- Header and corner selection; wheel and thumb scrolling; frozen quadrants while scrolling.
- Sheet switching by click and Ctrl+PgUp/PgDn (Data keeps its selection; chartsheet message); layout revalidation with `If-None-Match`; tile ring prefetch.
- Zoom 50% and gridlines off; ribbon stubs; File > Download; a 401 problem shown as a toast; devicePixelRatio 2 with forced colours.
- Median paint time 1.2 ms (max 3.6 ms) over 40 scroll frames at 1400×860.

deviations: render.js has no bitmap tile cache (§10 asks for LRU 64 per zoom/geometry version) and uses one canvas with four clipped quadrant passes instead of a canvas per quadrant. Reason: one 64×32 tile at default size is about 2048×1280 CSS px, 10 MB at DPR 1 and 40 MB at DPR 2, so 64 of them is 0.6–2.6 GB. Overflow text also crosses tile edges, so each bitmap would need its neighbours. Drawing the visible window directly measured a 1.2 ms median frame (max 3.6 ms) at 1400×860.
The data-tile LRU holds 256 tiles, as §10's frozen file list says. The task text said LRU 64, which I read as the render bitmap cache's number.
The sheet tab strip, Name Box and formula bar live in main.js for P1, because sheets.js and editor.js are later-phase files. P2 and P4 move them.

Mirror gridcells also carry data-x/y/w/h (the cell's canvas rectangle in CSS px), and the mirror and grid carry data-stale, data-pending, data-frame and data-loading markers. They let the Playwright check aim the pointer (P7's fill-handle drag needs this) and wait on state instead of timeouts.
Choices where §10 is silent:
- A sheet opens on the first cell past its frozen panes, as Ctrl+Home does.
- Home goes to the first unfrozen column.
- A whole-column or whole-row selection grows to hold the merges it crosses, as Excel does.
- A touch drag pans; a tap selects.
- A mouse click on a ribbon command returns focus to the grid; a keyboard activation does not.
open: Contract question for A (§8.3/§4.2): with defaults.columnWidth 8.43, the §4.2 formula gives 59 px, but Excel's default column is 64 px, which is file width 9.140625. Either `defaults.columnWidth` must be in `<col width>` units (padding included) or the client must add padding. The UI applies the formula as specified.

Contract gap (§8.3 tile `fill`): the tile says which `*x` character to repeat but not where the format placed it. The renderer repeats it before the text, so Accounting-style `"$"* #,##0.00` pads before the `$` instead of after it. It needs a position, or split text, in the tile cell.
`workbook.activeSheet` is read as a sheet key, falling back to the first visible sheet; §8.3's example cannot tell a key from an index. Please confirm with A.
Text rotation (alignment.rotation) is not rendered in P1.

Not in P1: Ctrl+G/F5 Go To (dialogs.js), the long-poll change feed (sync.js; tiles.invalidate and the ETag revalidation path are ready and unit-tested), editing, clipboard, menus and status-bar aggregates.

Only one Chromium run: a 304 answered to a script-set If-None-Match shows up in Playwright's requestfailed event as net::ERR_ABORTED, while fetch resolves with status 304. check.js exempts exactly that case; P7's scripts/check_excel_ui.py should do the same.

findings.issue: Extent::add (line 208) and Extent::remove (line 226) index the 16,384-entry counter box unchecked, so caller input can panic. `Sheet::cell_mut` (line 491) lets a caller replace the cell wholesale, so `*sheet.cell_mut(a).unwrap() = cell.clone().at(CellRef::new(0, 20000))` puts a cell in a row it no longer sorts into. A later `remove_cell(CellRef::new(0, 20000))` or `slice(..)` then panics with 'index out of bounds: the len is 16384 but the index is 20000'. I confirmed this with a probe linked against the built rlib. Before P1a the same misuse only mis-wrote a cell and never panicked. AGENTS says caller input never reaches a panic. The `cell_mut` rustdoc promises 'the cell stays where it is' but nothing enforces it. Separately, the replaced cell also breaks the row's sort order, so binary search and `dimension()` go wrong.
findings.fix: Make Extent panic-free: use `columns.get_mut(column as usize)` in `add` and `remove` and skip counters outside the box. Then either (a) hand out a guard from `cell_mut` that restores `reference` on drop, or (b) state in the `cell_mut` rustdoc that the reference must not change, and add a test that replaces a cell through `cell_mut` with an out-of-grid `.at(..)` and then calls `remove_cell`, `slice` and `write_xml` without panicking.

findings.issue: `cell_under` formats the refusal with `{error}`, which is now `ExcelError`'s Display. For an `Unrecognized` error cell the message says `got the error #UNRECOGNIZED` instead of the literal the file held (`#FUTURE!`). The probe output was `invalid record value at E!A1: expected a float64 value, got the error #UNRECOGNIZED`. The old code printed the literal. The 'actual' value in the refusal is now wrong.
findings.fix: Format with `cell.error_text()` instead of the enum: `got the error {}`, `cell.error_text()`. Add a declared-field read test over an unrecognized-error cell that asserts the literal appears in the message.

findings.issue: `Cell::move_to` (crate-private, line 1234) repeats the body of the public `Cell::at` (line 1140), which now has no in-crate caller. One fact, two owners.
findings.fix: Keep one mover: write `at` as `self.move_to(reference); self`, both `const`. Or make `move_to` the only crate-side mutator and keep `at` as its consuming wrapper.

findings.issue: The `Row` rustdoc says 'a row costs one allocation whatever it holds'. That holds only for a row read from a part, which gets an exact-capacity vector. A row built with `set_cell` or `write_serie` grows by `Vec::insert` doubling (4, 8, 16, ...), so a 40-cell row costs about five allocations. The doc states a cost the code does not have.
findings.fix: Reword to 'one vector of cells, exact-capacity when read from a part'. Optionally pre-size the row vector in `write_serie` (`Vec::with_capacity(columns.len())` on row creation) so the built path matches.

findings.issue: The held-state bounds the `Sheet` rustdoc states have no counting-allocator pin: the single 64 KiB extent box per non-empty sheet, none for an empty one, and no extras entries for cells stating no `cm`/`vm`/`ph`. AGENTS requires held-state bounds to be asserted in the counting allocator. `excel_cell_is_at_most_80_bytes` pins only sizes. `excel_sheet_parse_costs_nothing_per_cell` shows the cost is flat in width but does not show that the extent is one box or that extras stay empty. Also, `rust/tests/excel/sheet.rs:1247` never asserts that a sheet parsed from a part reports `revision() == 0`. The §2.3 dirty rule (`revision != saved`) depends on exactly that, and I only saw it hold via a probe.
findings.fix: Add an allocations row: `Sheet::new` allocates nothing, the first `set_cell` adds the extent box once, and further cells in one row add nothing beyond the row vector's growth. Add a second row (or extend the parse pin) showing that parsing a sheet with no `cm`/`vm`/`ph` allocates no extras nodes. Add to the sheet tests: `Workbook::from_bytes(..).sheet(..)` has `revision() == 0`, and it stays 0 after a `sheet_mut` that changes nothing.

findings.issue: `ZipArchive::copy_member_from` is a new public verb with a stated call-count cost, but it has no `holder` benchmark row (`rust/benchmarks/holder/zip.rs`) and no docs entry (the ZIP signature block near `docs/holder/index.md:5455` and its cost model). AGENTS: every surface touched gets tests, a benchmark and a docs entry. Design §12.2 schedules neither, so no later phase will add them.
findings.fix: Add the benchmark row and the docs signature and cost line in P1b, where the carry loop first calls it, or in P12. If P1b lands them together, put both in that phase's file set.

findings.issue: Interim style write-back for P1b: the guard `own < self.style_offset` treats `style_offset` as the count of the package's own `cellXfs`. `Styles::spliced` (styles.rs:325-331) returns the position of an already-spliced run of the six crate formats, not the count. For a crate-written package that was later extended in Excel, the run sits at 0, so every non-temporal style Excel added is dropped on rewrite. Separately, in-range indices from another workbook are written blindly, as are `cm`/`vm` (already listed under `open` for P1b). `Sheet::set_cell`/`put` also resets a replaced cell's StyleId to DEFAULT, which the design's edit path (§4.3, P4) must carry over.
findings.fix: In P1b replace the guard with the written styles part's real `cellXfs` count and reset `StyleId`s and cm/vm extras when the sheet's `origin` differs from the target workbook. Have P4's `set_entries` keep the replaced cell's style.

findings.issue: The report says the `iobase_calls` excel row moved and was re-pinned. The diff shows only the new zip test `copying_a_member_moves_its_encoded_bytes_a_batch_a_call_and_decodes_nothing` in that file. No excel row in `iobase_calls.rs` changed. The handoff misstates a cost pin, and AGENTS says a moved count is a design answer.
findings.fix: Correct the handoff: only the `allocations` excel rows were re-pinned, and no `iobase_calls` excel count moved. If one did move, the re-pinned assertion and its reason are missing from the diff.

findings.issue: The style write-back guard `own < self.style_offset` uses the wrong bound whenever the opened styles part already holds this crate's six-format run. `Styles::spliced` (styles.rs:322-331) then returns the position of that run as `offset`, not the count of the part's cellXfs. Proven with a probe: write a workbook with the crate, append a 7th `<xf>` to `xl/styles.xml` (count 6 to 7), set `s="6"` on B1, reopen, `set_cell(C1)`, write. B1 comes out with no `s`, and the styles part written still holds all 7 xfs. For a package the crate wrote, the run is at 0, so `own < 0` never holds and every non-temporal style is dropped. That is the ordinary second-generation file: crate-written, styled in Excel, then edited by the crate. The phase's headline behaviour, a cell keeping the style the file gave it, fails there. The existing test `a_cell_keeps_the_style_the_file_gave_it_through_an_edit_of_another_cell` covers only the first-splice case, where `offset == cellXfs count`. The doc on `write_xml` ("below `style_offset`") states the wrong contract.
findings.fix: Thread the count of the opened part's own cellXfs, separate from the crate-format offset. Have `Workbook::styles_for_write` (workbook.rs:687) return `(bytes, offset, styles.len())`, using 0 for the fresh package. Pass it through `Sheet::write_xml` and the two call sites (workbook.rs:728 and 793), and guard with `own < own_xfs` instead of `own < style_offset`. `Styles::len()` is `formats.len()`, which is correct in both the first-splice and re-splice cases. Add a test that reopens a crate-written package whose styles part gained an xf after the run, and asserts `s` survives an edit of another cell. Also state on the public `Cell::with_style` and `Cell::style` docs (cell.rs:1133) that a style is written only when it names one of the opened part's own xfs and a temporal cell writes the crate's format instead. As written, `with_style` on a fresh workbook silently does nothing.

findings.issue: `Extent::add` and `Extent::remove` index `columns[column as usize]` on a `MAX_COLUMNS`-long box with no bound check. A cell whose column is out of grid can reach the sheet through the public `cell_mut`, because `Cell::at` and `Cell::new` are public and unvalidated. Reproduced: `*sheet.cell_mut(A1).unwrap() = Cell::new(CellRef::new(0, 20000), ..)` followed by `sheet.remove_cell(CellRef::new(0, 20000))` panics with `index out of bounds: the len is 16384 but the index is 20000`. The old BTreeMap-keyed layout could not panic here. The same assignment also desyncs the sorted-vector, extent and extras invariants: `dimension()` and `cell_count()` become wrong and the binary search can miss cells. `cell_mut` is documented as leaving the reference to the sheet, but nothing enforces it.
findings.fix: Make `cell_mut` unable to move the cell. Either return a small guard type that derefs to `Cell` and restores `move_to(original_reference)` on `Drop`, or replace it with `update_cell(reference, impl FnOnce(Cell) -> Cell)` that applies `.at(reference)` to the result. At minimum use `columns.get_mut(column as usize)` in `Extent::add` and `Extent::remove` so a stray reference cannot panic. Add a test for the assignment case.

findings.issue: Unverified against Excel, and interim until P2. A dynamic-array anchor's `cm` is now written back, but the formula is written as plain `<f>` because `t="array"` and `ref` are dropped. Pinned output: `<c r="A1" cm="1"><f>SEQUENCE(2)</f><v>1</v></c>`. That is metadata declaring a dynamic array on a cell whose formula is not an array formula. Before this phase both were dropped, which gave a consistent legacy formula. Excel may repair or drop the record. The test pins the inconsistent state as the expected output.
findings.fix: Until P2 carries `t`/`ref` in `CellExtra.formula`, do not write `cm` on a cell whose formula the writer emits without its array attributes, or open the file in Excel to confirm it loads clean. Move the `cm` pin in `what_a_few_cells_state_beside_their_value_moves_with_the_cell_and_goes_with_it` to P2 with the formula attributes.

findings.issue: An error cell whose file literal is empty (`<c t="e"/>` or `<c t="e"><v></v></c>`) reads as `ExcelError::Unrecognized` carrying the literal `""`, so `error_text()` answers `""`. That contradicts the docs, which say `#UNRECOGNIZED` for no literal and the empty text only for no error. It is written back as `<c t="e"><v></v></c>`, an error cell with an empty `<v>`. A formula with no cached value, `<c t="e"><f>X</f></c>`, becomes `<f>X</f><v></v>` the same way. The write behaviour is the same as before this phase, but this phase defines the `Unrecognized` semantics.
findings.fix: In `Sheet::read_cell` (sheet.rs, around 1092), treat an error-kind cell with an empty trimmed literal as a cell with no error and no value: `Cell::new(reference, CellKind::Number, format, Scalar::Null)`, keeping its formula. Alternatively refuse it. Either way, add a parser and sheet test for `<c t="e"/>` and `<v></v>`.

fixed.summary:
I checked all 12 review findings against the code. Nine were real and are fixed, each with a test. Two are deferred with a named owner. One was a misstatement in the handoff.

1. MAJOR, Extent panic plus `cell_mut` desync: fixed.
   - `Extent::add` and `Extent::remove` now use `columns.get_mut(..)`. A counter outside the 16,384-entry box is skipped, not indexed, so the edge scans stay in range.
   - `Sheet::cell_mut` now returns a new public guard, `excel::CellMut<'_>`, instead of `&mut Cell`. The guard implements Deref and DerefMut to `Cell`, and its Drop calls `move_to(original reference)`. This is the same idea as `BinaryHeap::peek_mut`, and it is re-exported from `excel/mod.rs`.
   - New test `a_cell_borrowed_through_cell_mut_is_back_at_its_reference_whatever_was_put_there` assigns a cell moved to column 20000 through the guard. It checks the reference, count and dimension are restored and that `slice` still works. It then `mem::forget`s a guard and runs `remove_cell`, `slice`, `dimension`, `set_cell` and a package write, with no panic.
2. MINOR, `cell_under` printed `#UNRECOGNIZED` instead of the literal: fixed. It now formats with `cell.error_text()`. Test: `a_declared_column_refuses_an_unrecognized_error_by_the_literal_the_file_held`, which expects the message to end "got the error #FUTURE!".
3. MINOR, `at` and `move_to` both set the reference: fixed. `Cell::at` is now `self.move_to(reference); self`, both const.
4. MINOR, `Row` doc claimed one allocation per row: fixed. The doc now says the vector is exact-length when read from a part and grows as a vector grows when built cell by cell. I did not pre-size the vector in `write_serie`.
5. MINOR, missing held-state pins: fixed.
   - New `allocations` row `excel_sheet_holds_one_box_of_column_counts_and_its_rows` pins these counts:
     - `Sheet::new`: 0
     - first cell: 3 (the column box, the rows-map node, the row vector)
     - cells 2 to 4 in the same row: 0
     - fifth cell: 1
     - a cell in a new row: 1
     - replacing a cell: 0
     - first cell after emptying the sheet: 2 (the box is taken again; the emptied map keeps its root node)
   - `excel_sheet_parse_costs_nothing_per_cell` now also parses the same sheet with `ph` on every cell (repacked with `copy_member_from`). That costs at least 256*40/11 more allocations, which proves plain cells hold no extras entry.
   - New sheet test `a_sheet_read_from_a_part_is_at_revision_zero_until_it_changes` shows revision 0 after parse, and still 0 after a `sheet_mut` whose calls change nothing.
6. MINOR, no benchmark row or docs for `copy_member_from`: deferred, listed under open. `rust/benchmarks/holder/zip.rs` and `docs/holder/index.md` are not in P1's file set.
7. MINOR, style write-back for sheets from another workbook: partly covered by the fix to finding 9. The part about another workbook's styles (the `origin` reset) and `set_cell` resetting the style belongs to P1b and P4, listed under open.
8. MINOR, handoff said an `iobase_calls` excel row moved: that statement was wrong. `git diff` of `iobase_calls.rs` is 60 added lines, all in the new zip test, and no excel row changed. Only `allocations` excel rows were re-pinned.
9. MAJOR, style guard used the wrong bound: fixed.
   - New crate-private `WrittenStyles { offset, own }` in `sheet.rs`. `Workbook::styles_for_write` returns it, with `own` taken from the new `Styles::len()` (the number of `cellXfs`) and zero for a package built from nothing.
   - `write_xml` and both call sites take it, and the guard is now `own < styles.own`.
   - Test: `a_package_this_crate_wrote_keeps_the_styles_excel_added_after_its_formats`. The crate writes a package, the test appends a 7th xf, sets `s="6"` on B1, reopens and edits C1. B1 keeps `s="6"`, A1 keeps its temporal style, and `cellXfs` stays at count 7, so the formats were not added twice. The test failed with the old guard; I checked this by putting the old guard back temporarily.
   - The `Cell::with_style` and `Cell::style` rustdoc now say when a style is written.
10. MINOR, the same out-of-grid panic as finding 1: fixed by finding 1.
11. MINOR, `cm` written beside a plain `<f>`: fixed as interim. `PartWriter` leaves `cm` out when the cell writes a formula, because array attributes are not written until P2. `cm` is still held in extras and still written on cells with no formula. The pin in `what_a_few_cells_state_beside_their_value...` now expects `<c r="A1"><f>SEQUENCE(2)</f><v>1</v></c>` and a comment names this interim behaviour.
12. MINOR, empty error literal: fixed.
   - `Sheet::read_cell` reads an error cell whose trimmed literal is empty (`<c t="e"/>`, `<v></v>`, `<v> </v>`, or a formula with no cached value) as a Number cell holding null, and keeps its formula.
   - `Cell::with_error(Unrecognized)` treats an empty text as no literal.
   - Tests: parser `an_error_cell_stating_no_error_is_a_cell_holding_nothing`, sheet `an_error_cell_stating_no_error_holds_nothing_and_is_written_back_as_no_error` (no `t="e"` in the output, `<c r="C1"><f>NEXT()</f></c>`), and a new cell.rs assertion that an empty literal gives `#UNRECOGNIZED`.
